installer: set cr50 board id before update Make sure the cr50 board id is set before updating cr50. We have implemented cr50 factory mode. Cr50 may enable factory mode if the board id isn't set. We need to make sure everytime chromeos tries to update cr50 it first attempts to set the board id, so we don't accidentally enable factory mode on legacy boards. This change modifies the installer to set the board id before updating cr50. It will set the board id to RLZ:'unknown' phase flags. On new boards the factory will set the board id with the correct phase. This script will only set the board id on any board that didn't get the board id set. cr50: Disabling TPM or enabling TPM. This patch introduces a new firmware status, TPM mode along with a new TPM vendor command VENDOR_CC_TPM_MODE. TPM mode indicates whether TPM is enabled or disabled. Initially, this value shall be TPM_MODE_ENABLED_TENTATIVE, which means TPM is enabled but can be changed. VENDOR_CC_TPM_MODE changes this value either as TPM_MODE_ENABLED or TPM_MODE_DISABLED. This is for one time use only until next TPM reset event. Once TPM is disabled, any subsequent TPM commands shall fail. TPM_MODE_TPM_MODE command may be issued with input size as zero, which would not change TPM mode value. Either with the valid input value or without any input value, it returns the current TPM mode value in uint8_t type. This adds 160 bytes in binary. cr50-result: set board id before updating Board id should be set before we update to a new cr50 image. If cr50-result decides not to set board id it will still update cr50. It is important to set board id before updating cr50 because it will protect PVT devices from updating to prePVT images. Setting board id before update will also prevent factory mode cr50 images from entering factory mode. Erased board id is part of the factory mode requirement, so if we set the board id before update, cr50 won't accidentally enter factory mode. cros-go.eclass: add support for fetching and unpacking Go packages. It is getting very tedious having to mirror github.com repositories on chromium Gerrit for each new third party Go package we want to import. We'll soon end up with hundreds of these mirrors if we keep going in this direction. Adding an ebuild for a Go package on github.com should be as simple as specifying the repo path, commit hash, and a list of packages to install. Specifically, mirroring the repo should be unnecessary. cros_ec: fix the case of unavailable eraser After recent flashrom changes it was discovered that trackpad firmware updates on Eve are failing with no suitable erase function found in the flash descriptor. Further investigation has shown that when cros_ec.c:cros_ec_probe_size() creates a flash chip descriptor at run time, none of the created entries covers the entire chip (as expressed by erase_size * num_blocks). This does not prevent the programmer from programming the entire chip, and needs to be further investigated. This patch keeps track of the available eraser descriptions and uses the largest available descripor as a fallback when no valid (i.e. covering the entire chip) descriptors are found. b/110474116 has been opened to investigate the issues with creating the run time flash descriptor in case of Cros EC programming.
